# Triage inbound requests: Notion

**Pattern:** Ticket Triage · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers escalation work end to end across Notion, Slack, Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Normalize Ticket Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Delegate 'bug' to Sub-workflow
5. Fast-Track 'billing' + Alert
6. Fast-Track 'howto' + Alert
7. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
8. Merge Routed Work
9. Fingerprint for Idempotency
10. Drop Already-Processed Items
11. Enrich with Reference Data
12. Fold In Enrichment Fields
13. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
14. Archive Row Snapshot
15. Stamp Completion Time
16. Persist Run Metadata
17. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
18. Record Sub-workflow Result
19. Load Previous Snapshot
20. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
21. Stamp Processing Time
22. Guard Non-Empty subject
23. Save Execution Metadata
24. Sort Tickets Newest First
25. Cap Batch Volume
26. Align Field Names
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Microsoft Teams

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing escalation work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Normalize Ticket Payload → Route by Work Type → Delegate 'bug' to Sub-workflow → Fast-Track 'billing' + Alert → Fast-Track 'howto' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty subject → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Tickets Newest First → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Microsoft Teams → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Slack aligned by hand for escalation
- Pushing escalation events into Notion and Slack the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Escalation work where "Normalize Ticket Payload" is still a manual step before Notion
- Escalation work that only reaches Notion when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Slack in step for escalation, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Slack are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this escalation build
- A failed Notion or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this escalation build
- Branches rejoin before Notion, so a escalation run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every escalation run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Notion

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
escalation payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your escalation process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
